headline: Bitcoin is down about 15% this week after hitting its lowest price since September 2024 on Friday, as a sell-off in AI stocks and expectations of a December Fed rate hike weighed on markets.

market.asOf: BTC read by this desk from CoinMarketCap at about 03:55 UTC Sat 21 Nov (10:55 Bangkok). ETH from Bitcoin.com News at 8:33pm ET Friday (01:33 UTC); CoinMarketCap's ether page showed about $1,733, roughly 7% higher, so sources disagree. SOL not confirmed this run. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Two readings, both deep in fear: TokenPost reported the Fear & Greed index at 12 out of 100 in an article published 03:00 UTC Sat, and CoinMarketCap's own index showed 8 out of 100 when this desk read it Saturday morning Bangkok time.

stories.title: Bitcoin heads for a 15% weekly loss after its lowest price since September 2024
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to $57,799 on Friday, its lowest price since September 2024, and is down about 15% on the week. Traders who borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced out, and money kept leaving US bitcoin funds. Ether fell even harder.
points: Bitcoin's Friday low was $57,799.29, per Bitcoin.com News; it is down about 15% on the week and 31% on the month, and more than half below its record of $126,080 set in October 2025.

Ether traded at $1,618.84 at 8:33pm ET Friday (08:33 Sat Bangkok), down 8.11% on the day, with $427.5 million of ether bets wiped out in 24 hours, 87.7% of them bets on higher prices, per Bitcoin.com News.
Bets wiped out in 24 hours across crypto were about $1.5 billion per CoinGlass data cited by CoinDesk, and $1.9 billion per Bitcoin.com News; the sources differ.

US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $582.2 million on Thursday 19 Nov, led by $541.1 million from BlackRock's IBIT, per The Block; November's outflows are near $3.5 billion. Friday's figure was not out when this was written.
Strategy (MSTR) closed Friday at $77.80, its lowest close since February 2024 and about 30% lower on the week, per Bitcoin.com News.

stories.title: AI stock rout: Nvidia drops 14% and all three US indexes are in a correction
stories.summary: US stocks fell hard on Friday after reports of an SEC accounting investigation into chipmaker Nvidia, per The Motley Fool. An investigation is not a finding of wrongdoing. Crypto has been trading like a risky tech stock, so bitcoin and bitcoin miners fell with the chip stocks. US stock markets are closed for the weekend, so these are Friday's closing numbers.
points: Nvidia closed at $125.53, down 14.01%; AMD fell 13.26% and Broadcom 12.12%, per The Motley Fool.
The Nasdaq fell 5.3% to 22,617.73, the S&P 500 3.7% to 6,910.39 and the Dow 1.9% to 48,147.33, leaving all three more than 10% below their record highs, per Bitcoin.com News.
Bitcoin miners were hit hard: Hut 8 fell about 15%, and CleanSpark, Core Scientific and Bitdeer each fell more than 13%, per CoinDesk.

Anthropic, which closed its first trading day Thursday at $97.17 after an $83 IPO price, fell more than 8% on Friday, per Bitcoin.com News; CoinDesk reported it down more than 14%, so the sources differ.

stories.title: Markets price a December Fed rate hike as almost certain
stories.summary: The Fed meets on 8-9 December, and markets expect it to raise interest rates, not cut them. The only open question is whether it raises by a quarter point or a half point. Higher rates make cash and government bonds pay more, which makes assets that pay no interest, like bitcoin and gold, less attractive.
points: Reuters reported CME FedWatch odds of about 99% for a quarter-point hike, per FinanceFeeds; Seoul Economic Daily put the odds at about 90% for a quarter point and 10% for a half point after Fed Governor Waller raised the idea of a bigger move. The sources differ on the split, but neither shows any real chance of no change.
At the October meeting the Fed held its rate at 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack voting for a hike, per the Fed's minutes.
Gold fell as low as $3,513.54, its lowest since September 2025, and lost about 8% on the week, per FinanceFeeds.
The 10-year US Treasury yield is near 5%, per FinanceFeeds.

briefs.title: Binance hackers move about $860 million in ether
briefs.summary: Elliptic says about 488,000 ETH left the largest hack wallets from 17 to 20 Nov, and at least 2,310 BTC, about $149 million, has gone through mixers, per Bitcoin.com News.

briefs.title: Wrapped Monero token crashes after an exploit
briefs.summary: Wagyu's XMR1 token fell from nearly $500 to under $1 in about 30 minutes; Bitquery estimates about $13.5 million was drained. Monero itself was not breached, per Bitcoin.com News.

briefs.title: Coinbase plans its own prediction markets
briefs.summary: Bloomberg reports Coinbase is aiming to launch in-house prediction markets in the first half of 2027; Coinbase did not confirm the timeline, per Bitcoin.com News.

briefs.title: Saylor: Strategy could sell bitcoin to defend its preferred stock
briefs.summary: Michael Saylor says Strategy could shrink its STRC preferred stock toward $5 billion through buybacks, and could sell bitcoin to fund those buybacks under some market conditions, per Bitcoin.com News.

briefs.title: Ether funds bleed too
briefs.summary: US spot ether ETFs lost $131.24 million on Thursday, $124.22 million of it from BlackRock's ETHA, per Bitcoin.com News citing SoSoValue.

briefs.title: JPMorgan: bitcoin trades far below its mining cost
briefs.summary: JPMorgan estimates it costs about $86,000 to produce one bitcoin and says "some capital has also left the crypto market altogether," per The Block.

briefs.title: Crypto tax bill may get a House vote
briefs.summary: Rep. Horsford wants a House vote on the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, which cleared committee 38-5, before this Congress ends, per The Block.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: October inflation (PCE) and Q3 GDP are both due at 8:30am ET, per the BEA schedule. Core PCE consensus 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per Newsquawk; forecasters including RBC put headline PCE near 3.8% (prior 3.6%). Q3 GDP growth expected at 3.5% against the 3.4% first estimate, per Trading Economics. Jobless claims move up a day for Thanksgiving.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per the Fed's calendar. October new home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok), per the Census Bureau.
On Friday 27 Nov US stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per Admiral Markets. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.
Settles at 08:00 UTC, per MEXC. TokenPost puts the Deribit bitcoin expiry at about $6.67 billion across 105,053 contracts, with the "max pain" level at $74,000 (read 20 Nov).
Fed officials stop public comment on policy until after the December meeting, per Admiral Markets.
The last jobs report before the Fed decision, per the BLS schedule. JOLTS job openings come out Tue 1 Dec at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok); November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed.
